classification.difficultyReason: Directly apply the vertical line test to four familiar graph shapes, identifying whether any input has two outputs.

content.prompt: Which of the graphs below represent functions?

spec.description: Right-opening sideways parabola with vertex at the axes' intersection and arrows on both branches. No numerical scale, ticks or grid.
spec.mathematics: A representative unscaled sideways parabola x proportional to y squared.
spec.answerVisibility: Entire figure is supplied in the student question.

answer.worked: A vertical line to the right of the vertex intersects the graph twice. The graph fails the vertical line test.

spec.description: Upward-opening V with its vertex on the negative y-axis and arrows at both upper ends. No numerical scale, ticks or grid.
spec.mathematics: Each x-value has exactly one y-value.
spec.answerVisibility: Entire figure is supplied in the student question.

answer.worked: Every vertical line intersects the graph exactly once. The graph passes the vertical line test.

spec.description: Unfilled diamond centred at the axes' intersection, with all four vertices on the axes. No numerical scale, ticks or grid.
spec.mathematics: The upper and lower vertices give two distinct y-values at x equal to zero.
spec.answerVisibility: Entire figure is supplied in the student question.

answer.worked: The vertical line through the centre intersects the diamond at its upper and lower vertices. The graph fails the vertical line test.

spec.description: Decreasing concave-up curve crossing the positive y-axis and approaching the positive x-axis from above, with arrows at both ends. No numerical scale, ticks or grid.
spec.mathematics: A representative unscaled exponential decay curve preserving the source's graphical relationships.
spec.answerVisibility: Entire figure is supplied in the student question.

answer.worked: Every vertical line intersects the curve exactly once. The graph passes the vertical line test.
